# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Traynard_2020_remifentanil"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Traynard_2020_remifentanil"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12500> (open access)

Traynard et al. (2020) is a CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology
tutorial on the MonolixSuite workflow. It builds a population PK model of
remifentanil step by step, starting from a two-compartment model (run PK_01)
and ending with the final model PK_16. The final model has three compartments,
power effects of age on CL, Q2, Q3 and V3, and of lean body mass (LBM) on CL
and V1, a sex effect on V3, correlated random effects on (CL, Q3, V3) and on
(Q2, V2), and a proportional residual error. The main text describes the final
model but does not print its parameter table. The estimates come from the
authors' deposited Monolix project (Supporting Information, Supinfo 2), file
`final_workflow/PK_16/populationParameters.txt`.

# Population

The tutorial re-analyses the publicly available remifentanil data set of
Minto et al. (Anesthesiology 1997;86:10-23; reference 7 of the tutorial). It
holds dense concentration measurements from 65 healthy adults after a single
constant-rate intravenous infusion of 1-8 ug/kg/min lasting 4-20 min, 1992
concentrations in all. Ages range from 20 to 85 years and lean body mass from
36.5 to 75.6 kg; 27 subjects are female and 38 male.

The same data set ships with R as `nlme::Remifentanil`. The maintainers
checked it against the deposited tutorial file `PK_reminfentanil.csv`
(Supinfo 2): every subject's infusion rate, total dose, age, LBM and sex match
exactly, and both hold the same 1992 concentrations. This vignette therefore
uses `nlme::Remifentanil` as the observed data.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Traynard_2020_remifentanil")()$population`.

# Source trace

Unless noted otherwise, every value comes from the deposited final run
`final_workflow/PK_16/populationParameters.txt` (Supinfo 2). Monolix reports
`omega` as the SD of the normal random effect on the log scale, so the
variances in `ini()` are `omega^2` and each covariance is the correlation
times `omega_i * omega_j`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: 3-compartment, i.v. infusion, linear elimination | n/a | Main text 'Final model overview'; `PK_16.mlxtran` uses library model `infusion_3cpt_ClV1Q2V2Q3V3` |
| `lcl` (CL, L/min) | log(2.56943) | `Cl_pop` |
| `lvc` (V1, L) | log(4.85867) | `V1_pop` |
| `lq` (Q2, L/min) | log(0.0825548) | `Q2_pop` |
| `lvp` (V2, L) | log(7.59029) | `V2_pop` |
| `lq2` (Q3, L/min) | log(1.92566) | `Q3_pop` |
| `lvp2` (V3, L) | log(8.20430) | `V3_pop` |
| Age centering `log(AGE/36.6299)` | 36.6299 years | Main text, covariate section; `PK_16.mlxtran` `[COVARIATE]` |
| LBM centering `log(LBM/55.1554)` | 55.1554 kg | `PK_16.mlxtran` `[COVARIATE]` |
| `e_age_cl` | -0.320405 | `beta_Cl_logtAGE` |
| `e_lbm_cl` | 0.410657 | `beta_Cl_logtLBM` |
| `e_lbm_vc` | 1.26150 | `beta_V1_logtLBM` |
| `e_age_q` | -0.950579 | `beta_Q2_logtAGE` |
| `e_age_q2` | -0.869000 | `beta_Q3_logtAGE` |
| `e_age_vp2` | -0.462430 | `beta_V3_logtAGE` |
| `e_sex_vp2` (male vs female, log scale) | 0.271176 | `beta_V3_SEX_1`; SEX coding 1 = male, 0 = female from Supinfo 1 'Data set' |
| `etalcl`, `etalq2`, `etalvp2` block | omega 0.142692, 0.412362, 0.313035; r(Q3,Cl) 0.675947, r(V3,Cl) 0.709079, r(V3,Q3) 0.821229 | `omega_Cl`, `omega_Q3`, `omega_V3`, `corr_*`; main text Table 1 rows PK_12, PK_13 |
| `etalq`, `etalvp` block | omega 0.385790, 0.853822; r 0.650297 | `omega_Q2`, `omega_V2`, `corr_V2_Q2`; main text Table 1 row PK_15 |
| `etalvc` | omega 0.264638 | `omega_V1` |
| `propSd` | 0.112461 | `b`; main text 'Error model' (proportional error, run PK_16) |

The deposited runs agree with the numbers quoted in the main text. Run PK_02
has `omega_Cl` = 0.228 and run PK_03 has 0.164 (main text: "decreased from
0.228 to 0.164"). Run PK_15 has an additive error `a` = 0.00076 with an RSE of
209% (main text: "a = 0.00076 ... RSE for a is high (209%)").

# Observed data and event table

```{r data}
remi <- as.data.frame(nlme::Remifentanil)

subjects <- remi |>
  group_by(ID) |>
  summarise(
    amt = sum(Amt),
    rate = first(Rate),
    AGE = first(Age),
    LBM = first(LBM),
    SEXF = as.integer(first(Sex) == "Female"),
    WT = first(Wt),
    HT = first(Ht),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    tinf = round(amt / rate),
    tinf_group = cut(
      tinf,
      breaks = c(0, 6, 9, 12, 30),
      labels = c("4-5 min", "7-8 min", "10 min", "14-20 min")
    )
  )

# The LBM column is the James formula from weight, height and sex.
james <- with(
  subjects,
  ifelse(SEXF == 1, 1.07 * WT - 148 * (WT / HT)^2, 1.1 * WT - 128 * (WT / HT)^2)
)
stopifnot(max(abs(james - subjects$LBM)) < 0.01)

dose_rows <- subjects |>
  transmute(
    id = ID, time = 0, amt, rate, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
    AGE, LBM, SEXF, tinf_group, obs_conc = NA_real_
  )
obs_rows <- remi |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  transmute(id = ID, time = Time, obs_conc = conc) |>
  left_join(subjects |> select(id = ID, AGE, LBM, SEXF, tinf_group), by = "id") |>
  mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

c(subjects = nrow(subjects), observations = nrow(obs_rows))
table(subjects$tinf_group)
```

# Known-answer check against the Monolix population predictions

Monolix writes the population prediction `popPred` for every observation
(`final_workflow/PK_16/predictions.txt`, Supinfo 2). It is the model solved
with all random effects at zero and each subject's own covariates. The rows
below cover young and old subjects of both sexes, at the end of infusion and
in the terminal phase. Both sides use the same parameters, so any difference
is numerical error, and the check uses a tight bound.

```{r known-answer}
mod <- readModelDb("Traynard_2020_remifentanil")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega")

solve_quiet <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

pred <- solve_quiet(
  mod_typical,
  events = events,
  keep = c("obs_conc", "tinf_group"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  as_tibble()

monolix_poppred <- tribble(
  ~id, ~time, ~popPred,
  24, 2.52, 30.1907,
  24, 18.13, 8.66205,
  24, 60.18, 0.272058,
  17, 7.03, 56.1953,
  17, 70.18, 0.23843,
  64, 3.99, 67.0946,
  64, 66.97, 0.12134,
  55, 4.06, 78.527,
  55, 67.24, 0.115821
)

ka_check <- monolix_poppred |>
  left_join(distinct(pred, id, time, Cc), by = c("id", "time")) |>
  left_join(subjects |> select(id = ID, AGE, LBM, SEXF), by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc / popPred - 1))

ka_check |>
  mutate(Cc = signif(Cc, 6), pct_diff = signif(pct_diff, 2)) |>
  rename(
    "Subject" = id, "Time (min)" = time, "Monolix popPred (ng/mL)" = popPred,
    "nlmixr2lib (ng/mL)" = Cc, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(nrow(ka_check) == 9, all(abs(ka_check$pct_diff) < 0.01))
```

# Population predictions against the observed data

```{r obs-vs-pred, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(pred, aes(Cc, obs_conc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Population prediction (ng/mL)",
    y = "Observed concentration (ng/mL)",
    title = "Observed vs population-predicted remifentanil",
    caption = "Population-prediction counterpart of the individual-prediction plot in Figure 3c."
  )
```

```{r ratio}
ratio <- pred |>
  filter(!is.na(obs_conc)) |>
  mutate(r = obs_conc / Cc)
ratio_summary <- c(
  median = median(ratio$r),
  q10 = unname(quantile(ratio$r, 0.1)),
  q90 = unname(quantile(ratio$r, 0.9))
)
signif(ratio_summary, 3)
# The fixed effects are centred on the data, so the median observed /
# predicted ratio sits close to 1. Deterministic: observed data and typical
# predictions involve no random draws.
stopifnot(abs(log(ratio_summary[["median"]])) < log(1.15))
```

```{r spaghetti, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(pred, aes(time, group = id)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = obs_conc), alpha = 0.3, size = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cc), alpha = 0.4, colour = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~tinf_group) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Remifentanil (ng/mL)",
    title = "Observed data (points) and population predictions (lines)",
    caption = "Layout after Figure 1a: one panel per infusion-duration group."
  )
```

# Visual predictive check

The stochastic simulation reuses the observed design (dose, rate, sampling
times and covariates of every subject), replicated three times (195 virtual
subjects). It is plotted as a prediction-corrected VPC with 10 time bins, as
in Figure 5a. The band is the simulated 5th-95th percentile and the line the
simulated median; the points are the observed median (filled) and 5th and
95th percentiles (open).

```{r vpc, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200212)
n_rep <- 3L
events_rep <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_rep), function(k) {
  events |> mutate(orig_id = id, id = id + (k - 1L) * 1000L, rep = k)
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(events_rep$id)) == n_rep * nrow(subjects))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_rep,
  keep = c("orig_id", "tinf_group"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(id, orig_id, tinf_group, time, sim)

bins <- quantile(pred$time, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 11))
pred_binned <- pred |>
  mutate(bin = cut(time, bins, include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(bin) |>
  mutate(pred_bin = median(Cc), pc = pred_bin / Cc) |>
  ungroup()

obs_pc <- pred_binned |>
  transmute(bin, time, pc_obs = obs_conc * pc)
sim_pc <- sim |>
  left_join(
    pred_binned |> select(orig_id = id, time, bin, pc),
    by = c("orig_id", "time")
  ) |>
  mutate(pc_sim = sim * pc)

summ <- function(x) {
  c(q05 = quantile(x, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), q50 = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q95 = quantile(x, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE))
}
bin_time <- pred_binned |> group_by(bin) |> summarise(t = median(time))
vpc_obs <- obs_pc |>
  group_by(bin) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(pc_obs, 0.05), q50 = median(pc_obs),
    q95 = quantile(pc_obs, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(bin_time, by = "bin")
vpc_sim <- sim_pc |>
  group_by(bin) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(pc_sim, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), q50 = median(pc_sim, na.rm = TRUE),
    q95 = quantile(pc_sim, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(bin_time, by = "bin")

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = vpc_sim, aes(t, ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = vpc_sim, aes(t, q50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = vpc_obs, aes(t, q50), colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data = vpc_obs, aes(t, q05), colour = "black", shape = 1) +
  geom_point(data = vpc_obs, aes(t, q95), colour = "black", shape = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Prediction-corrected remifentanil (ng/mL)",
    title = "Prediction-corrected VPC",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5a of Traynard 2020."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. The comparison below runs PKNCA on the observed
concentrations and on the stochastic simulation from the VPC section (three
replicates of the observed design, with between-subject variability and
residual error), using the same sampling times and grouped by infusion
duration. A time-zero row with concentration 0 anchors the AUC; the infusion
starts at time 0.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- function(df, conc_col) {
  out <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    transmute(id, time, conc = .data[[conc_col]], treatment = tinf_group)
  bind_rows(
    out,
    out |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)
  ) |>
    distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, time)
}

nca_intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
run_nca <- function(df) {
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(df, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, intervals = nca_intervals))
}

nca_obs <- run_nca(nca_input(pred, "obs_conc"))
nca_sim <- run_nca(nca_input(sim, "sim"))

nca_tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_sim,
  reference = nca_obs,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "min", auclast = "min*ng/mL", half.life = "min")
)
knitr::kable(
  nca_tbl,
  caption = "Median NCA: observed data (Reference) vs stochastic simulation of the same design (Simulated)."
)
```

`r if (!is.null(attr(nca_tbl, "footnote"))) attr(nca_tbl, "footnote")`

```{r pknca-check}
nca_median <- function(res) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
    group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(value = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}
cmp <- inner_join(
  nca_median(nca_obs) |> rename(observed = value),
  nca_median(nca_sim) |> rename(simulated = value),
  by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / observed - 1))
cmp
# Medians over 33-90 simulated subjects per group: robust to which subjects
# a given rxode2 build draws. The 4-5 min group (3 observed subjects) is
# excluded from the bound; see the text below.
big_groups <- cmp |> filter(treatment != "4-5 min")
stopifnot(nrow(big_groups) == 6, all(abs(big_groups$pct_diff) < 25))
```

In the three infusion-duration groups with 11 to 30 subjects, the simulated
median Cmax, AUClast and terminal half-life are close to the observed
medians. The 4-5 min group holds only 3 subjects (one 4-min and two 5-min
infusions), so its observed medians are dominated by individual
variability; its larger Cmax difference is not a sign of misfit.

# Covariate effects

```{r covariates}
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
typical <- expand.grid(AGE = c(20, 40, 60, 80), SEXF = c(1, 0)) |>
  mutate(
    CL = exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (AGE / 36.6299)^th[["e_age_cl"]],
    Q2 = exp(th[["lq"]]) * (AGE / 36.6299)^th[["e_age_q"]],
    Q3 = exp(th[["lq2"]]) * (AGE / 36.6299)^th[["e_age_q2"]],
    V3 = exp(th[["lvp2"]]) * (AGE / 36.6299)^th[["e_age_vp2"]] *
      exp(th[["e_sex_vp2"]] * (1 - SEXF)),
    Sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "female", "male")
  )
typical |>
  select(Sex, AGE, CL, Q2, Q3, V3) |>
  mutate(across(c(CL, Q2, Q3, V3), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Age (years)" = AGE, "CL (L/min)" = CL, "Q2 (L/min)" = Q2,
    "Q3 (L/min)" = Q3, "V3 (L)" = V3
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical parameters at LBM 55.2 kg.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Parameter source.** The main text gives the final model structure and
  covariate model but no table of final estimates (Figure 2b shows only the
  first run, PK_01). The values come from the authors' deposited
  `final_workflow/PK_16/populationParameters.txt`. The `<PARAMETER>` block of
  `PK_16.mlxtran` holds the *initial* values of that run (carried over from
  PK_15 with "Use last estimates") and was not used.
* **Sex encoding.** The data set codes SEX as 1 = male and 0 = female
  (Supinfo 1), and Monolix estimates the effect for SEX = 1 with female as
  the reference. The model stores the canonical `SEXF` (1 = female) and
  applies `exp(e_sex_vp2 * (1 - SEXF))`. The known-answer check above
  includes subjects of both sexes and reproduces the Monolix predictions.
* **Lean body mass.** The tutorial does not state how LBM was derived. The
  data set's LBM column reproduces the James formula from weight, height and
  sex (checked above), so users should compute LBM the same way.
* **Compartment naming.** The Monolix V2/Q2 pair maps to `vp`/`q`
  (`peripheral1`) and V3/Q3 to `vp2`/`q2` (`peripheral2`). In this fit the
  V2 compartment is the slowly equilibrating one (Q2 = 0.083 L/min).
* **Relation to Minto 1997.** The data are those of Minto et al. (1997), but
  this model is the tutorial's own Monolix fit, not a transcription of the
  model Minto et al. published.
* **Units.** Time is in minutes, doses in ug and concentrations in ug/L
  (= ng/mL), as in the tutorial data set; clearances are in L/min.
